title: Mod view: source maps and readable code

units.title: Literature review: recovering names for functions and data
units.detail: The mod view (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): generated code named from a source-map sidecar and printed readably, mostly for agents to read, on Emerald first. A deep review: read the primary papers and tool source (not summaries), add each to docs/references.md. Cover symbol recovery from decomps (pret's .map and .sym files, pret's symbols branches), function matching (IDA FLIRT, Ghidra Function ID, BinDiff, Diaphora), and learned naming (DIRTY, VarBERT, ReSym, GenNm and newer LLM work): what each needs as input, how it is scored, what accuracy it reaches. Say what fits us, where names change no behaviour and we can print the code any way we like. Write docs/research/name-recovery.md.

record.evidence: docs/research/name-recovery.md (653 lines): pret .sym/ELF/DWARF/.map measured on Emerald (names stable: 42 of 32,690 changed in a year; DWARF locals 70% in registers over 400 fns); FLIRT, Ghidra FID/BSim, BinDiff, Diaphora, WARP, decomp-toolkit, ds-decomp, objdiff read in source at pinned commits; DIRE, DIRTY, VarBERT, ReSym, GenNm, Debin, NERO, SymLM, XFL, SymGen, ReCopilot, REBENCH and others read as PDFs with input, metric and table numbers; fit for the mod view. references.md gains a Name recovery section. just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Exact names for Emerald from pokeemerald's symbols
units.detail: The mod view (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): generated code named from a source-map sidecar and printed readably, mostly for agents to read, on Emerald first. pokeemerald builds a byte-identical Emerald, so its symbol file gives the name and address of most functions and variables. Fetch pret's pokeemerald (symbols, and the source for later units) pinned by commit into $GBAA_DATA, as just fetch-tests does; never the ROM. Match its symbols to our discovered functions and to RAM/ROM data addresses, and report: how many of our 15,158 functions get a name, which pret functions we don't discover (and why), which of ours pret has no name for. Output a ground-truth names file the later units read (format is the design's; plain TOML is fine for now). Thumb bit and RAM-copied code (overlays) need care.

pokeemerald.elf has DWARF 2: locals/params with register or sp slot, struct types, file:line. binutils 15.2 readelf rejects it (.debug_abbrev 'not zero terminated'); Fedora gdb reads it (info scope FN, ptype, info line). One location per var, no loclists. See name-recovery.md

units.title: Design the mod view and its source map
units.detail: The mod view (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): generated code named from a source-map sidecar and printed readably, mostly for agents to read, on Emerald first. From the review and the pret matching, write docs/mod-view-design.md: the source map's format (functions, globals and ROM data by address; per-function names for registers and locals by address range; types later, if at all), where it lives and how a mod copy is cut; how the printer applies it with no change in behaviour, and the check that proves it; the readable print form for chosen functions (registers as locals via --locals, tick!/call!/ret! macros, quieter insn! comments, call return values if the calling convention can be trusted for that function); and the naming loop: what an agent sees per function, how it is scored against pret, the cap of a few hundred functions before june's look. Then check this group's units fit, edit, add or drop them. Ask june (just ask) about any choice that changes scope.

units.title: Spike: how close exact Rust gets to pret's C, 10 functions
units.detail: june 2026-10-26 (d/mod-view-prints-maintainable-rust-close-to-pret): the mod view's readable form aims at maintainable Rust near pret's C, not asm with names. Take 10 Emerald functions of varied shape (a leaf getter, a loop over an array, a call chain, a switch or jump table, struct field access, a u8/u16 arithmetic one; ClearBattleMonForms and SeedRngAndSetTrainerId among them). Prototype a printer path that emits the closest Rust it can while staying exact: timing and flags folded into macros or hidden, registers as locals, expressions folded, names from the source map, types and struct fields from pret's DWARF (gdb reads it, see docs/research/name-recovery.md), loop idioms recovered. Target shape for ClearBattleMonForms: fn clear_battle_mon_forms(g: &mut Game) { for i in (0..4).rev() { g.battle_mon_forms[i] = 0; } }. Check each prototype is exact (fn-diff or sst-gen on those functions, and the Emerald new-game route with them swapped in). Score each against pret's C: statements, named accesses, loop shapes, what's left as raw addresses or casts. Write the side-by-sides and scores into docs/mod-view-design.md, say what each gap would take (by technique, from the decompiler literature in name-recovery.md), and propose how the readable-form units ({unit:mod/readable-print}, {unit:mod/readable-exact}, {unit:mod/readable-emerald}) should change. Stop at ~3 h with what's measured.

units.title: call! writes lr and takes the callee's key itself
units.detail: From {unit:research/code-without-rom-addresses}: june wants fewer ROM addresses in the code. In call!(m, pc, f_08002065 @ 0x0800_2065 -> 0x0800_bc3f, 6, { regs!(m; …, 14 = 0x800_bc3f) }) the lr write repeats the return site and the @ key repeats the callee's name. Make call!/call_any! write lr from -> ret (codegen drops 14 = … from the sync when it equals ret|1) and take the entry key from the callee (a const next to each fn, or a table lookup at compile time), so a call reads call!(m, pc, f_08002065 -> 0x0800_bc3f, 6, …). Guest state must stay byte-identical: same-states and own-state-check on Kirby and Emerald, exact and instant, both print modes. Update docs/mod-view-design.md.

units.title: A call a mod adds needs no ROM address
units.detail: From {unit:research/code-without-rom-addresses}: a call a mod adds has no ROM return site, and today the editor must invent one. Give mods call!(m, f, …) with no addresses: lr gets a reserved key outside the GBA map (e.g. 0xF000_0000 + a per-mod-site index), the macro accepts that key as 'came back', and a restore or IRQ that has to resume at it is counted and reported like a mod resume today (docs/mod-view-design.md, 'Resumes'). Show it on a Kirby or moonbeam mod that calls a game function from a new place, with save, load and rewind inside the call.

record.evidence: call!(m, pc, f, {sync}) in a mod: lr gets a reserved per-site key above 0xF000_0000, registers restored, value r0; a guest-RAM record lets a lost frame rerun its block. mods/katam/half-speed (Kirby Amazing Mirror, GetInput waits an extra V-blank, game at half speed): state saved at frame 1001 inside the call, loaded, ran 300 frames, 'mod: 1 ... (1 at a call the mod added ...)'; rewind 1000+31 into the call, same count, ran to 1300; no fault. --unwind livelocks a call that always spans a frame end (documented). 3 runtime tests; just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Readable code shows the bytes behind ROM data pointers
units.detail: Stopgap for games whose text encoding nobody has worked out yet ({unit:mod/text-tables} found no table, {unit:mod/text-from-screen} hasn't run). We can't tell text from other data, so every pointer into ROM data the readable print loads gets its bytes shown as a fixed array of integers, marked encoding unknown: up to the next address other code points at, capped at a size cutoff (start around 32 bytes; record the cap in TOML). Display only: the generated code still reads the ROM, so mods and asset overrides keep working. Where a game's table is known, decoded text replaces the array. Done when a game with no table (e.g. WarioWare) shows the arrays in its readable print, a test covers the cutoff and the next-label stop, and the same-states check stays the same.

units.title: Decode other games' text with community encoding tables
units.detail: Most GBA games don't use ASCII: each maps bytes to its own font tiles. The ROM-hacking community has ready-made tables (.tbl files on Data Crystal, romhacking.net) for most well-known games. Load a per-game table (kept outside the repo like the ROMs, path recorded in TOML; note each table's source) and reuse {unit:mod/text-emerald}'s printing. Try it on the ROMs we have: Kirby & the Amazing Mirror, Minish Cap, Metroid: Zero Mission, WarioWare. Done when, for each game with a table found, the readable print shows text that matches a screenshot of the same scene, with a written list of the games where no table turned up or the text is compressed.

units.title: Readable code shows Minish Cap's text by message number
units.detail: Minish Cap looks its text up by a message number (MessageFromTarget(index), ShowTextBox(textIndexOrPtr); gTranslations[lang] -> bank offsets -> string, ASCII, 00 ends), not by pointer, so the pointer decoding of {unit:mod/text-tables} finds nothing real there. Decode a call's constant index argument through gTranslations with tmc's charmap (crates/codegen/text-tables.toml lists it, reached = "index") and comment the call with the string. Done when a readable print's comment matches a screenshot of the same text box.
